a41591a.body:
fix: repair installer hook drift, harden guards, add Bash write detector

The installer hardcoded its hook list, so it shipped a tree that did not
match the manifest: 6 of 7 scripts copied (session-start.sh silently
missing) and 4 of 6 events registered. Both lists are now derived from
hooks.json, and tools/test-installer.sh grows a parity group that fails by
name when the installed tree drifts from canonical.

Three guards were passing on inputs they should have caught:

- stop-guard.sh scanned raw JSONL with regex and never checked role, so a
  claim quoted by the user counted as the assistant's own. It now parses
  each line as JSON, gates on assistant role, and requires PROOF citations
  to resolve to a real file under e2e-evidence/ or evidence/.
- fresh_evidence.py validate returned OK on zero-artifact runs, unsealed
  runs, and equal-size substitution. The inventory is now v2 with SHA-256
  per artifact, strict hex, duplicate and traversal rejection, and a
  count/total cross-check. Legacy v1 inventories fail closed.

Bash-authored writes bypass the PreToolUse guards entirely, because those
match Write|Edit. This adds detection, not prevention: bash-write-snapshot.sh
hashes protected paths before a Bash call, bash-write-notice.sh re-hashes
after and reports what changed. It never denies.

Detection is by effect, never by parsing the command. An earlier attempt
parsed shell to decide a deny and falsely blocked cp -p, mv -f, touch -c and
sed -i -e; that approach was abandoned. A command that changes nothing emits
nothing, so no false positive can interfere with a working command. Content
hashing rather than mtime+size is what catches cp -p and equal-size
substitution of a protected artifact.

The bypass itself remains open and is documented as open. Closing it needs
central enforcement that does not read shell.

Also: 18-skill router head verified to reach all 17 targets, architecture
doc written, and stale counts corrected across README, plugin README and
INSTALL.

Verified: tools/test-hooks.sh (10 detector cases, mutation-proven),
tools/test-installer.sh (10 groups incl. canonical parity, mutation-proven),
tools/dry-run-install.sh, tools/verify-orchestration.py, tools/build-site.py

e8d46fb.body:
feat: prove two more hooks in live sessions; scope claims to evidence

Adds stop_guard and instructions_loaded probes. Five probes now pass
with the plugin loaded and fail without it.

instructions_loaded has real attribution: the plugin arm appends 30
JSONL lines resolving to the run's cwd, the control arm appends 0. Byte
growth was not enough — other hooks write to the same file, so the
probe snapshots the line count and parses only what this run added.

stop_guard is deliberately scoped: hook_response records carry the
EVENT name ("Stop"), never the script filename, so it proves the Stop
event fired and its hooks exited success — not that stop-guard.sh
specifically ran. That script is silent unless it blocks, so a clean
turn emits nothing attributable. Recorded as a limit, not claimed as
proof.

Writing these found a fourth false-pass trap: loads_this_run compared
/tmp/... against the tap's /private/tmp/... because macOS resolves /tmp
through a symlink. The lines were always from this run; the comparison
was wrong.

79d9dc3.body:
feat: add SDK end-user probe harness; fix two documented-flag defects

The repo had no way to prove the plugin works. tools/test-hooks.sh runs
one hook script in isolation, which says nothing about whether the host
loads the plugin, surfaces its skills, or fires its hooks.

tools/sdk_probe.py drives a real Claude session via claude-agent-sdk
with the plugin loaded, and runs every probe twice — with and without
the plugin. Three probes pass loaded and fail unloaded. Two are
UNPROVEN and reported as such: the SDK session advertises no Write
tool, so the PreToolUse guard cannot be exercised end to end.

Writing the control arms found three ways the probes could pass while
proving nothing: text matching (the model read SKILL.md off disk with
Bash), bare skill names (all 17 also exist standalone in
~/.claude/skills), and a Skill invocation that had actually failed (the
model retried with the bare name). Each is now checked.

Also fixes two defects found by inspection:
- commands/truth-audit.md documented --since/--until; the script it
  drives takes --start/--end, so every documented invocation failed.
- commands/rate-prompt.md omitted --ship-below-threshold.
- tools/build-site.py had undeclared PyYAML and pandoc dependencies;
  both now fail fast with an install hint, and are documented in
  tools/INSTALL.md.
